materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.content_note: Walk-through of one ES futures trade across 10 numbered steps plus a closing multi-timeframe summary. Uses a Market Delta chart, NYSE TICK, 3-minute bars and 1-minute ES volume. Covers: momentum low on expanded volume; no-trade rules ('I don't sell markets that make new highs and I don't chase highs on dwindling volume'; 'I don't chase sellers'); candidate highs; selling on positive TICK / green Market Delta that cannot make fresh price highs; stop above candidate highs (new highs invalidate); target of range lows; cover on volume pickup and very negative (-1000) TICK; explicit target limitation (play for highest-probability move, not a home run breakout); long waiting/observing behavior; multi-timeframe applicability focus list.
materials.content_type: official blog post (step-by-step trade walk-through; ES futures)
materials.diversity_role: market context / observed cue / watching-no-trade / confirmation / invalidation / exit / target-limitation / applicability

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.content_note: Classifies most trading patterns into three basic setups: 1) Reversal trades (market at/beyond a trading-range edge, cannot sustain buying/selling interest, falls back; initial target generally range midpoint or prior pivot; good volume + extreme NYSE TICK frequently tests the opposite end; especially watch reversals in weak relative volume - market-maker driven markets); 2) Breakout trades (range-bound market surges out on enhanced volume + very high/low NYSE TICK; usually a catalyst; cross-market repricing as confirmation; daily price targets R1/R2/R3 / S1/S2/S3); 3) Continuation trades (trend in place, wait for pullback; volume expands with trend and contracts on pullbacks; trending cumulative NYSE TICK and Market Delta; TICK/Delta pullbacks as entries; e.g. hit R1, light-volume pullback -> reload long for R2).
materials.content_type: official blog post (setup taxonomy: reversal / breakout / continuation)
materials.diversity_role: market context / observed cue / confirmation / applicability / exit-target conventions

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.content_note: Short post using a range-day read in ES futures. Covers: opening-range context and sensitivity to a range day; important sectors (XLE, XLF) not confirming the upside breakout while XLB and XLV looked sketchy at the highs; failure to take out the prior day's high; re-entering the morning range; recognizing the upmove was failing without needing to catch the exact top; playing a reversion back to VWAP as a first target; closing process claim 'Making the hard trade: It's all about preparation.'
materials.content_type: official blog post (failed-breakout / range-day market read; ES futures + sector confirmation)
materials.diversity_role: failure / non-confirmation / invalidation / exit-target (reversion to VWAP) / review-process

selection_basis_note: Selection based on provenance + free/public access + anchor quality + failure/no-trade coverage + extraction suitability. NEVER based on expected trading performance, backtest quality, or ease of producing a strategy.

free/public/unauthenticated access state (verified by direct fetch on 2026-08-19)

stable attributable URL, title, and post date
